method: Instruction listings decoded directly from the PE bytes of the identified executable through its section table, with the executable size and SHA-256 verified first. Every cited instruction address, operand, name literal, holder vftable cell, type descriptor name, RTTI name and call target was compared with those listings. Callers were enumerated by scanning the .text section for rel32 call and jmp instructions, so virtual and indirect callers are not covered. Addresses are absolute virtual addresses. No decompiled body is a tracked evidence dependency.
scope: Static Lua call contracts of the thirteen natives that control the player input counters, the camera and the opening tutorial waits: _lockCameraControl, _unlockCameraControl, _isCameraControlEnabled, _isPlayerControlEnabled, _isLockonControlEnabled, _forceCameraTPSMode, _cancelAimCameraTutorial, _cancelLookAtPlayerTutorial, _waitForCharaSchedulerTutorialFinished, _aimCameraChocobo, _cancelAimCameraChocobo, _waitForTargetTutorial and _waitForCameraTutorial. Each row gives the registration site, receiver type check, declared argument and return lists, reads, client state effects, failure behavior and yield behavior. Client-side contracts do not establish camera presentation, tutorial content or server behavior.
evidenceTier: MIXED, see tierVocabulary and the tier of each fact

tierVocabulary.STATIC: Read directly from instructions or data at the cited addresses.
tierVocabulary.INFERRED: A name or role assigned from the surrounding instructions. The bytes do not state it.

framework.reference: manifests/zone_in_native_call_contract.json framework and manifests/fade_actor_group_native_call_contract.json framework: registration, the 0x00CC9D60 type registry, argument marshalling, the holder receiver adapter, the world object chain and the yield request.

worldObject.chain: R is the address that 0x00CC7510 returns for ExecuteParameters +0x04. X = [R], Y = [X +0x04] and W = [Y].

fields.W (Y +0x00): Object whose first dword is V. The tutorial walks and the Chocobo natives use it.
fields.Z (Y +0x04): Target cursor receiver of the global contract.
fields.Y +0x08: Object whose first dword is V. The control natives use it.
fields.V +0x17838: Object E whose +0x7C dword leads to the camera object.

rows.callbackKind: thunk through a receiver vftable slot
rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x128 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine calls 0x0075B2D0, which jumps through slot 10 of the RaptureUserControl at V +0x17758. That slot looks up the object with the identity 0xC0000004, calls virtual slot 2 of three named command objects when the lookup succeeds and adds 1 to the camera counter at object +0x54. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x128]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD5F2C holds 0x006DEA60, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD7984 holds 0x006E33C0.
The MyPlayer routine resolves the world chain, loads the dword at Y +0x08 and calls 0x0075B2D0 on it.

0x0075B2D0 loads V, takes the RaptureUserControl at V +0x17758 through 0x004D7580 and tail jumps through its virtual slot 0x28 (slot 10), 0x0054B680. The routine returns the new counter in EAX and the callback ignores it.

0x0054B680 looks up the object registered under the identity 0xC0000004 through 0x004D9910 on the container stored at object +0x04. When the lookup returns an object it takes the address object +0x08 and, for each of the three command names RaptureCommands.MoveCamera, RaptureCommands.ForwardCameraOff and RaptureCommands.BackwardCameraOff, finds the command object through 0x00928F90 and calls its virtual slot 2 with three arguments: a temporary built by 0x0052D3A0 from 0 and 0, that address and 0. It then adds 1 to the dword at object +0x54 whether or not the lookup found an object.
The counter at +0x54 is a camera lock depth, by the native names and because _isCameraControlEnabled reads it. The effect of virtual slot 2 on the three command objects was not traced.

rows.callbackKind: thunk through a receiver vftable slot

arguments.note: Optional. A Nil cell leaves the value false.

rows.behavior: Tail-jumps through slot 0x200 of the receiver vftable. The PlayerBase routine is a bare return. The MyPlayer routine reads an optional bool, false for a Nil cell, resolves the world chain and tail calls 0x0075C740 on W with it. A true value sends the record 0x2D with the payload 1 to the camera object at V +0x4C4. A false value sends the record 0x10 with the payload 0 to the object that the container at +0x7C of V +0x17838 holds at +0x4C4, when it exists. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback is the thunk 'mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x200]; jmp eax'. The PlayerBase vftable 0x00FD5E04 cell 0x00FD6004 holds 0x00776340, a bare 'ret 4'. The MyPlayer vftable 0x00FD785C cell 0x00FD7A5C holds 0x006E6570.

The MyPlayer routine stores a zero byte, compares the tag byte of cell 0 with 6 and, for any other cell, reads the byte through 0x0071BA00. It then resolves the world chain and jumps to 0x0075C740 with ECX set to W and the byte as the stack argument.

0x0075C740 loads V. A nonzero byte calls 0x004D7320, which returns the dword at V +0x4C4, and jumps to 0x0055C560 with the value 1. 0x0055C560 sends the record number 0x2D with a 4 byte payload holding 1 through 0x004D7980. With the rule of the fade contracts that the routine adds 0x15 to the record number, the scene packet type is 0x42.

A zero byte takes the dword at V +0x17838 through 0x004D72F0 and calls 0x00586F20 on it. That routine loads the dword at object +0x7C, takes its dword at +0x4C4 through 0x004D7320 and, when it is nonzero, calls 0x0055F230. 0x0055F230 sends the record number 0x10 with a 4 byte zero payload, scene packet type 0x25.

The camera object at V +0x4C4 is the object that _waitForCameraTutorial and the Chocobo camera natives use. That the dword at object +0x7C of the V +0x17838 object is V is INFERRED from the shared +0x4C4 accessor. The consumers of the records 0x2D and 0x10 and the class of the camera object were not traced.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, runs the prelude and the name number walk of _aimCameraTutorial and then undoes the aim state. It calls 0x0075F070 with the flag 0, 0x0075C720 and 0x0075B700 with the cursor index 0. The identity that the walk finds is not read again. It pushes no value and requests no yield.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0, resolves the world chain, calls 0x0075D120 on the object at Y +0x110 with ExecuteParameters +0x04. The global contract records that routine, which refreshes the dword at V +0x500. It builds the iterator 0x007176C0 with ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the int and runs the node walk 0x00764150 on W.

After the walk the callback calls 0x0075F070 on Z = [Y +0x04] with 0, then 0x0075C720 on W, then 0x0075B700 on Z with 0. It destroys the iterator with 0x00717730. No instruction reads the identity at iterator +0x0C.

0x0075F070 takes the cursor state S from V +0x4C0 through 0x004D7310, walks the cursor vector at S +0xA8 and calls 0x00563510 on each non-null cursor with the flag. This is the worker of _setAllTargetCursorMask.
0x0075C720 takes S and, when the dword at S +0xC0 is not 0xC0000000, calls 0x00561BB0 on S with 0. _aimCameraTutorial calls the same routine with 1.
0x0075B700 takes S and calls 0x00562D30 with the cursor index and a null chara. That is the worker of _setTargetCharacter, which the aim native calls with the found chara.
The native clears the cursor mask and target that _aimCameraTutorial set. The effects of 0x00561BB0 and 0x00563510 were not traced.

arguments.note: Name number of the chara that the walk searches.
Scheduler number that the checker tests on the found chara.

rows.behavior: Reads two ints, runs the prelude and the name number walk of the tutorial natives and builds a 0x0C byte s_WaitForCharaSchedulerTutorialFinishedResumeChecker that holds the found chara and the second int. It requests the yield with that checker without a condition. The checker ends the wait when 0x0058AB60 on the chara and the second int returns false. It pushes no value.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 into EBX and cell 1 into EBP through 0x005819A0, resolves the world chain, calls 0x0075D120 on the object at Y +0x110 with ExecuteParameters +0x04. The global contract records that routine, which refreshes the dword at V +0x500. It builds the iterator 0x007176C0 with the first int and runs the walk 0x00764150 on W.

It calls 0x0075C400 on W with a result slot, the address of the identity at iterator +0x0C and the second int. That routine resolves the identity through 0x004D9970, stores the chara at result +0x00 and the int at result +0x04.

The callback allocates 0x0C bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the checker with 0x007177B0 from the result slot, which stores the chara at checker +0x04 and the int at +0x08, and calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 with ExecuteParameters +0x08. No instruction between the construction and the request tests a condition.

The checker has the vftable 0x00FD58FC and the RTTI name s_WaitForCharaSchedulerTutorialFinishedResumeChecker. Its poll slot 0x00717880 calls 0x00758CE0 on checker +0x04, which calls 0x0058AB60 on the chara with the int. A returned 1 stores the waiting result 0x0130CECC. Any other value stores the done result 0x01377ECC. Its push slot 0x00A72A20 pushes nothing.

0x0058AB60 asks 0x00585800 for a group number from the constant 5 and the int, then calls 0x00589F60 with the group and the int. That routine searches the table of lists at chara +0x878, in groups 1 to 0x19, for an entry whose dword at +0x10 equals the int. 0x0058AB60 returns whether the result is nonzero.

The wait ends when the chara no longer holds the scheduler entry that _runCharaSchedulerTutorial started with the same number. A null chara from the walk reaches 0x0058AB60 without a test, and its effect was not traced. Whether 0x00CD2860 polls the checker once before it suspends was not traced.

arguments.note: Actor class number that the iterator compares with the work value 0x1389 of each NpcBase chara.

rows.behavior: Reads one int and builds an s_CharaIterateActorClass with it. After the node walk it calls 0x0075CDE0 on W with the found identity. That routine takes the object E at V +0x17838, sends the camera aim records through 0x00586E80 and calls 0x004D7890 on E with 0. It pushes no value and requests no yield. No prelude 0x0075D120 runs.

facts.claim: The callback reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0, resolves the world chain, loads W and builds the iterator 0x007178D0 (vftable 0x00FD590C, RTTI s_CharaIterateActorClass) from ExecuteParameters +0x04 and the int. It runs the walk 0x00764150, calls 0x0075CDE0 on W with the address of the identity at iterator +0x0C and destroys the iterator with 0x00717940.

Slot 1 of the iterator, 0x007179A0, resolves each identity, casts it to NpcBase (type descriptor 0x012709E4) and accepts a chara whose byte at +0x5C is nonzero. It reads the work value with the key 0x1389 through 0x00CC7B90 with the default -1 and compares it with the int at iterator +0x08. A match stores the identity at iterator +0x0C and stops the walk.

0x0075CDE0 takes E from V +0x17838 through 0x004D72F0, calls 0x00586E80 on it with the identity dword and then 0x004D7890 on it with 0. 0x00586E80 takes the object at +0x7C of E, reads its dword at +0x4C4 through 0x004D7320 and, when it is nonzero, calls 0x0055F2B0 on it with the identity, 0 and floats. 0x0055F2B0 sends the record number 9 with a 0x14 byte payload that holds the identity, the dword 2 and floats, then the record number 0x12 with the 4 byte payload 0x0A. The scene packet types are 0x1E and 0x27.

0x004D7890 stores its argument in the byte at E +0x90 and builds a message of type 0x11 for the argument 0 and 0x10 for any other argument through 0x004EC080. It hands the message to virtual slot 3 of the object at E +0x84.

The native points the camera at the NpcBase chara of the actor class, by the native name. A walk that finds nothing leaves iterator +0x0C at 0, and 0x00586E80 then sends the identity 0. The consumers of the records and the class of E were not traced.

arguments.note: Name number of the chara whose selection ends the wait.

rows.behavior: Reads one int, runs the prelude and builds a 0x0C byte TargetTutorialResumeChecker that holds the DesktopWidget receiver and the int. It stores the checker pointer at the receiver +0x6C and requests the yield without a condition. The wait ends when the routine at 0x006FE960 reports a chara whose name number equals the int. An int of 0 leaves checker +0x08 at 0, so the poll reports done at once. It pushes no value.

facts.claim: The callback resolves the world chain, calls 0x0075D120 on the object at Y +0x110 with ExecuteParameters +0x04. The global contract records that routine, which refreshes the dword at V +0x500. It then reads cell 0 through 0x005819A0.

The callback allocates 0x0C bytes through 0x009D1B35, constructs the checker with 0x00713A50 from the receiver and the int, stores the pointer at the receiver +0x6C and calls the yield request 0x00CD2860 with ExecuteParameters +0x08. No condition precedes the request.

The checker has the vftable 0x00FD5350 and the RTTI name DesktopWidget TargetTutorialResumeChecker. Its poll slot 0x00713AC0 stores the done result 0x01377ECC when the dword at checker +0x08 is 0 and the waiting result 0x0130CECC otherwise. Its destructor 0x00718E90 clears the dword at the widget +0x6C.

0x00718EF0 takes the chara record at chara +0x60 and maps the first dword -1 to 0. When it equals the checker int, it clears the widget +0x6C, clears checker +0x04 and stores 0 in checker +0x08, which ends the wait. Its only rel32 caller, 0x006FEAF2, lies in the routine at 0x006FE960, whose receiver holds the checker pointer at +0x6C. That routine passes a Utf8String built from the literal _onTargetChanged at 0x00FD47D8 to 0x00CC7A90, and its only rel32 caller is 0x008A3EB3.

The wait ends when the player targets the chara with that name number and the routine at 0x006FE960 is the DesktopWidget target changed handler, by the checker, the call site, the shared +0x6C field and the _onTargetChanged literal. The engine path behind 0x008A3EB3 and the other writers of checker +0x08 were not traced.

ledgerCandidates.note: These are the rows of the unimplemented ledger that this record gives a registration, argument list, return list, receiver check and callback contract. A client that implements them still needs the target cursor and look-at workers behind 0x00561BB0, 0x00563510 and 0x00587EF0, the consumers of the camera records, the writers of the camera tutorial bit at K +0x17C and the engine path that reports the targeted chara to the DesktopWidget.

boundaries: These are static client observations. No live Lua call or retail-client walk was performed.
Each registrar has one rel32 caller in .text, recorded as registrarCaller. The run-time order of registration is the switchboard order.
Script call-site counts are static presence in the shipped scripts. They do not establish which natives a given script reaches at run time.

The PlayerBase natives are thunks through the receiver vftable. The behavior recorded for them belongs to the MyPlayer override. A PlayerBase receiver that is not a MyPlayer takes the empty base routine.
The three waits request the yield without a condition. Whether the request routine 0x00CD2860 polls the checker once before it suspends was not traced.
The effects of the virtual slot 2 calls on the three camera command objects, the scene records 9, 0x10, 0x12 and 0x2D and the camera object class were not traced.
The prelude 0x0075D120 and the node walk 0x00764150 are recorded in manifests/global_native_call_contract.json. The identity that the cancel natives find is not read afterward.
